title: C# Questions & Answers - Enumerations
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on enumerations of C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Choose the correct statements about enum used in C#.NET?

options.text: An enum variable cannot have a private access modifier
An enum variable can be defined inside a class or a namespace
An enum variable cannot have a protected access modifier
An enum variable cannot have a public access modifier

questions.explanation: An enum type may be declared in a namespace or nested in a class. Nested enums may be private, protected, public, or internal; top-level enums may be public or internal. So 'cannot have a protected access modifier' is false.

questions.question: Which among the following cannot be used as a datatype for an enum in C#.NET?

options.text: short
double
int
all of the mentioned

questions.explanation: An enum underlying type must be a built-in signed or unsigned integer (byte, sbyte, short, ushort, int, uint, long, ulong). double and float are not allowed.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: sunday monday tuesday

questions.explanation:
Unspecified members continue from the previous value by +1. sunday = -3, so monday is -2 and tuesday is -1.

Output:

-3
-2
-1

questions.question: What will be the correct statement of the following C# code?

options.text: byte value cannot be assigned to enum elements
enum elements should always take successive values
enum must always be of int type
When the valid range of byte exceeds, the compiler will report an error

questions.explanation: The underlying type is byte (0–255). 500, 1000, and 1300 are outside that range, so the compiler reports an error. An enum may skip values and need not be int.

questions.question: Wrong statement about enum used in C#.NET is?

options.text: An enum can be declared inside a class
An object cannot be assigned to an enum variable
An enum can be declared outside a class
An enum can have Single and Double values

questions.explanation: The underlying type of an enum cannot be float or double (Single/Double). Enums may be declared inside or outside a class. You cannot assign an arbitrary object to an enum variable without a conversion.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: compile time error

questions.explanation: It will report an error since enum element cannot be assigned a value outside the enum declaration.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
Unspecified members continue from the previous value: green is 1, brown follows pink = 10 so brown is 11.

Output:

1
11

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: a
letters.a

questions.explanation:
Console.WriteLine of an enum value prints its name by default.

Output:

a

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: black
red

questions.explanation:
Enum.GetNames returns the member names in declaration order, so index 0 is red.

Output:

red

questions.question: Choose the correct statement about enum used in C#.NET?

options.text: By default the first enumerator has a value equal to the number of elements present in the list
Values of the enum elements cannot be populated from database
The value of each successive enumerator is decreased by 1
An enumerator has a white space in its name

questions.explanation: Enum members are named compile-time constants; you do not fill the enum definition from a database. By default the first member is 0 and each next is +1. Names cannot contain whitespace.

questions.question: Which among the following differentiates enum in C#.NET from enum in C language?

options.text: C is strictly a typed language, C#.NET also is a strictly typed language
In C, language variables of enum types can be used interchangeably with integers using type casts while enum variables cannot be used as a normal integers in C#.NET
None of the mentioned
All of the mentioned

questions.explanation: C# enums are strongly typed: you cannot treat them as int without a cast (and you cannot mix them as freely as in C). That is the main language difference among these options. Both C and C# are typed languages, so a is not a differentiator.
